_doc: Reviewed input for Namakkal's District Environmental Plan, prepared by the District Committee under the District Collector on the CPCB model plan and hosted on namakkal.nic.in. The figures below are transcribed from the water-relevant sections of the published PDF, each with the line it comes from and the page it sits on, so a reviewer can check every one against the document. The plan carries no NGT-template water-balance table (demand, supply, deficit), so waterBalance stays null; the figures are what the plan states, not a balance the Atlas computed. Oddities of the document are recorded in document.quirks rather than corrected.

document.title: District Environmental Plan, Namakkal District
document.publisher: District Collector, Namakkal, for the District Committee; members include the District Environmental Engineers, Tamilnadu Pollution Control Board, Namakkal and Kumarapalayam
document.editionNote: The cover is undated; the District Collector's signature on the last page is hand-dated 28/11/19, the PDF metadata creation date is 28 November 2019, and the upload path on namakkal.nic.in is 2019/11, so the edition is labelled 2019.
document.template: An Introduction (NGT order, District Committee membership, district profile) followed by twelve subject sections: solid, bio-medical, plastic and C&D waste, non-attainment cities, polluted river stretches, polluted industrial clusters, industrial pollution control, utilisation of treated sewage, conservation of water bodies, e-waste and illegal sand mining, each a short narrative followed by a responsibility / plan of action / stakeholders table or a work-to-be-carried-out / action-by table, with photograph pages between them. It prints no demand, supply or deficit water balance.
quirks: The cover cites Hon'ble NGT Order in O.A.No.710-713/2017 dated 15.07.2019, and the preamble the D.O. letter of 26.07.2019 that followed it, rather than O.A. 360/2018.

The cover prints the title on two lines, 'District Environmental Plan' over 'Namakkal District'; the comma in the title here is added. The cover carries two emblems and the motto 'Pollution Prevention Pays' but no office name in its text, so the publisher is taken from the District Committee list on page 4 and the 'District Collector Namakkal' signature block on page 38.
Every page carries a footer number equal to its PDF page number (the cover is page 1), so printedPage equals pdfPage throughout.
Village panchayats are counted as 322 on page 5 and 633 on page 16.

The 'status of water bodies' table on page 32 prints owner rows and column headings (available, rejuvenated in the past five years, under rejuvenation at present) but no counts; the work table below it starts at S.No 2.

The sampling-point table on page 20 is headed 'Ground water Sample Collection points' although the surrounding text describes river (GEMS and MINARS) and sewage-drain samples; Kokkarayanpettai appears twice (rows 5 and 6) with identical coordinates.
No district-level sewage generation figure is printed; the treated-sewage section gives the Tamil Nadu total and the consented capacities of two municipal STPs.
The solid-waste authorisation row on page 10 leaves its dates blank ('as on __ date').

Page 38 is a scanned signature page whose text layer is OCR ('District Cornnrittee', 'Governm.ent', 'A11 Municipal Commissioners'); the signature over 'District Collector Namakkal' is hand-dated 28/11/19.
The action tables carry no priority column, so every action point's priority is null.
Section 12 is headed 'Prevention Illegal Sand Mining'; the index lists 13 entries (Introduction plus the 12 subjects) while the conclusion says the plan covers '12 subjects'.

actionPoints.text: To carry out Air Quality Monitoring, Water Quality Monitoring (ground water) & Compost quality in and around processing facilities & dump sites as per Schedule I & II of SWM Rules, 2016
Special Task Force shall periodically review once in two weeks on the status of creating awareness and also on the prevention of dumping of solid waste and discharge of sewage in water bodies
Monitoring of industries by periodical collection of sewage/ Trade effluent Sample for ascertaining Water Quality
All the municipalities and Town Panchayat shall cover their entire jurisdiction area under UGDS scheme. Sewage received in STP shall be treated to the Discharge standards.
Periodic monitoring of treated sewage with preferably online monitoring (parameters for analysis pH, BOD, TSS, TDS, COD, Total N, Fecal Coliform)
Industries located near Common STP shall make MoU with the operator of STP so as to utilize treated sewage to meet their industrial requirement after proper tertiary treatment
Treated sewage from the Common STPs shall be utilized for industrial use, agriculture, ground water recharge and other non-domestic use
Collection of data regarding Sewage, Solid Waste disposal in river stretch with quality and prepare Digital Mapping with above details
Desilting, removal of enchroachments & flood control measures
Identification of river stretches where there are chances for illegal sand mining; frequent surprise checks in those river stretches by the Taluk Level Task Force, reporting fortnightly
